examples.en: Planes take off following instructions from the control tower.
The control tower and the pilot are communicating by radio.

examples.ko: 공항 관제탑이 한눈에 보이는 카페에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a cafe with a clear view of the airport control tower.
To work in a control tower, you have to pass an exam.

examples.ko: 관제탑은 활주로가 잘 보이는 높은 곳에 있어요.
examples.en: The control tower is in a high place with a good view of the runways.
I have an uncle who works in a control tower.

explain: 공항에서 비행기의 이착륙을 알려 주는 곳이에요. 뉴스에서는 조직의 중심 역할을 비유할 때 '컨트롤타워'라는 외래어도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the place at an airport that directs planes taking off and landing. In the news, the loanword '컨트롤타워' is also used as a metaphor for the central body of an organization.

en: of course; well, as for that

examples.en: Well, of course we should help.
Well, the teacher knows best, of course.

examples.ko: 그야 저도 가고 싶지만 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: Sure, I want to go too, but I don't have time.
Is it tasty? Well, you'll know when you try it.
Well, of course it's nice to have a lot of money.
Why was I late? Well, because the road was jammed.

explain: 대답이나 설명 앞에 붙여서 '그건 말할 필요도 없죠'라는 느낌을 줘요. '그야 당연하죠', '그야 그렇죠'처럼 굳어진 표현으로 많이 써요. '그야말로'(정말로)는 이 말과 다른 단어예요.
explain_en: Placed before an answer or explanation, it gives the feeling of 'that goes without saying'. It appears often in set phrases like '그야 당연하죠' and '그야 그렇죠'. '그야말로' (truly) is a different word, so don't mix them up.

p.n: 물론 is neutral and works in any register; 그야 adds a 'that goes without saying' tone.

examples.en: Since the fight, we act like strangers.
He was a stranger I met on the street, but I helped him.

examples.ko: 가족이어도 말을 안 하면 남남 같아요.
examples.en: Even family feels like strangers if you don't talk.
We share a family name, but we aren't related.

examples.ko: 한 집에 살아도 남남처럼 지내는 부부가 있어요.
examples.en: Some couples live in one house but act like strangers.

examples.ko: 남남끼리 만나서 가족이 되는 게 결혼이에요.
examples.en: Marriage is when two people who were strangers become a family.

explain: '타인'보다 부드러운 입말이고 '남이다'와 비슷하게 써요. 서로 가까운 사이였다가 멀어졌을 때도 '남남이 되다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: If we break up, we become strangers again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가깝던 사이가 완전히 끊어져서 아무 관계도 없게 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a once-close relationship is completely cut off.

explain_en: It is a softer spoken word than '타인' and is used like '남이다'. It is also used when people who were once close drift apart, as in '남남이 되다'.

examples.ko: 올림픽에서 한국 양궁은 단체전 금메달을 땄어요.
examples.en: At the Olympics, Korean archery won gold in the team event.
The team event is more nerve-racking than the individual event.
Our team came third in the team event.

examples.ko: 내일 단체전이 있어서 일찍 자야 해요.
examples.en: I have a team event tomorrow, so I have to sleep early.
Table tennis is divided into individual and team events.

examples.ko: 단체전은 한 명이 못해도 동료가 도와줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: In a team event, teammates can help out even if one person does poorly.

explain: 반대말은 '개인전'이에요. 양궁, 탁구, 체조처럼 한 종목 안에 개인전과 단체전이 같이 있는 경기가 많아요. 단체전은 팀 점수를 합쳐서 순위를 정하고, 뉴스에서는 '단체전 금메달'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is 개인전. Many sports, such as archery, table tennis and gymnastics, have both an individual and a team event. In a 단체전 the team's scores are added up to decide the ranking, and the news often says '단체전 금메달'.

en: to be lukewarm; to be tepid

examples.en: The bath water was lukewarm, so I heated it more.
The coffee cooled down and is lukewarm.
I drank a glass of lukewarm barley tea.
Don't answer that question in a half-hearted way.
It tastes bad if it's lukewarm, so I'll microwave it.
It rained, and even the air felt lukewarm.

explain: 뜨겁지도 차갑지도 않아서 어중간한 온도에 써요. 비슷한 말 '미지근하다'도 있고, 둘 다 온도뿐 아니라 시원하지 않은 반응이나 태도에도 말해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 기대만큼 뜨겁지 않고 별로 관심이 없는 반응을 말할 때 써요. 온도와 상관없이 쓰는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a reaction that isn't as enthusiastic as hoped. It is a figurative use unrelated to temperature.

explain_en: It is used for a temperature that is neither hot nor cold. A similar word is '미지근하다', and both can describe not only temperature but also a half-hearted reaction or attitude.

examples.ko: 그는 사업으로 젊은 나이에 백만장자가 됐어요.
examples.en: He became a millionaire at a young age through business.

examples.ko: 복권에 당첨되면 백만장자가 될 수 있을까요?
examples.en: If I win the lottery, could I become a millionaire?
When I was little, my dream was to be a millionaire.
I hear even millionaires eat instant noodles sometimes.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 평범한 사람이 백만장자가 되는 이야기예요.
examples.en: That movie is about an ordinary person who becomes a millionaire.

examples.ko: 백만장자의 하루를 보여 주는 방송을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a show about a day in the life of a millionaire.

explain: 백만장자는 돈이 아주 많은 사람이에요. 한국에서는 '부자'가 가장 평범한 말이고, '갑부'는 재산이 아주 큰 사람, '재벌'은 큰 회사를 가진 집안을 말해요. 백만장자는 외국 이야기나 영화에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 백만장자 is a person with a great deal of money. In Korea 부자 is the plain everyday word, 갑부 is someone with enormous wealth and 재벌 is a family that owns big conglomerates. 백만장자 shows up more in foreign stories and movies.

en: to make up for; to supplement

examples.en: I made up for the weak parts and submitted it again.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 단점을 계속 보완하고 있어요.
examples.en: This app keeps improving on its weaknesses.
I practice every day to make up for my weakness.
Please submit after you supplement the plan.

examples.ko: 보안 문제를 빨리 보완해야 한다는 의견이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Some said the security problem must be fixed quickly.
We work while covering each other's weak points.

explain: '부족한 점, 약점, 단점'을 목적어로 자주 받아요. 잘못된 것을 바로잡는 '고치다'와 달리, 있는 것에 모자란 부분을 채운다는 느낌이에요. 발음이 비슷한 '보안'(안전 지키기)과 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It often takes objects like shortcomings, weaknesses, or flaws. Unlike '고치다', which corrects something wrong, it feels like filling in what is lacking. Do not confuse it with the similar-sounding '보안' (security).

examples.en: Wild ginseng is much more expensive than regular ginseng.

examples.ko: 산에서 산삼을 캤다는 소문이 마을에 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: A rumor spread through the village that someone had dug up wild ginseng in the mountains.

examples.ko: 아버지가 산삼 한 뿌리를 선물로 받으셨어요.
examples.en: My father received a root of wild ginseng as a gift.
People who dig for wild ginseng are called simmani.

examples.ko: 이 약재에는 산삼 성분이 들어 있다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this herbal medicine contains wild ginseng.

examples.ko: 어젯밤 꿈에서 산삼을 봤는데 느낌이 좋아요.
examples.en: I saw wild ginseng in my dream last night and I have a good feeling.

explain: 밭에서 키운 것은 '인삼', 산에서 저절로 자란 것은 '산삼'이에요. 산삼은 구하기 어려워서 값이 아주 비싸고, 캐는 사람은 '심마니'라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: Ginseng grown in a field is 인삼, while ginseng that grows by itself in the mountains is 산삼. 산삼 is hard to find, so it is very expensive, and the people who dig for it are called 심마니.

examples.en: When I catch a cold, I drink ginger tea.
Slice the ginger thinly and put it in.
Some people don't like the smell of ginger.
Ginger goes well with meat dishes.
Ginger is spicy, but it warms the body.
I boiled ginger and jujubes together.

explain: 생강은 '생강차', '생강청', '생강 쿠키'처럼 향과 매운맛을 내는 재료로 많이 써요. 마늘, 파와 함께 기본 양념으로 들어가고, 몸이 차거나 감기 기운이 있을 때 차로 마시는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: Ginger gives scent and heat in things like 생강차 (ginger tea), 생강청 (ginger syrup), and ginger cookies. It is a basic seasoning alongside garlic and green onion, and people often drink it as tea when they feel cold or a cold coming.

examples.en: That friend was a well-known brawler in the neighborhood.
He looks like a fighter, but he is actually soft-hearted.
The quarrelsome man is quiet today.
I am not a fighter but a peace lover.
The fighter in the movie looked so cool.
You must not get in between the fighters.

explain: '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 자주 하거나 잘하는 사람에게 붙어요. 싸움꾼은 싸움을 잘하거나 자주 하는 사람이라 칭찬보다는 조금 부정적인 느낌이에요. 말다툼을 자주 하는 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '-꾼' attaches to a person who often does or is good at something. A 싸움꾼 is someone who fights well or often, so it sounds a bit negative rather than praising. It can also be used for someone who often argues.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어릴 때 양부모를 만났어요.
examples.en: That child met his adoptive parents when he was little.
On the weekend, I greeted my adoptive parents for the first time.
The adoptive parents raised the child with great care.
She visited Korea again with her adoptive parents.

examples.ko: 양부모의 사랑 덕분에 잘 자랐다고 말했어요.
examples.en: He said he grew up well thanks to his adoptive parents' love.

examples.ko: 입양된 후 양부모 곁에서 학교에 다녔어요.
examples.en: After being adopted, she went to school living with her adoptive parents.

explain: 입양해서 키워 주는 부모를 말해요. 낳아 준 부모는 '친부모'나 '생부모'라고 하고, 높일 때는 '양부모님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means the parents who adopt and raise a child. Birth parents are called '친부모' or '생부모', and the polite form is '양부모님'.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 장대높이뛰기 세계 기록을 세웠어요.
examples.en: That athlete set a world record in the pole vault.
I saw the pole vault for the first time at a sports day.
The pole vault looks really hard technically.

examples.ko: 올림픽 장대높이뛰기 결승을 보느라 밤을 샜어요.
examples.en: I stayed up all night watching the Olympic pole vault final.
My younger sibling won a gold medal in the pole vault.

examples.ko: 장대높이뛰기도 배울 수 있는 학원이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a place where I can learn the pole vault too?

explain: 긴 장대를 이용해 바를 넘는 육상 종목이에요. 장대 없이 뛰어서 넘는 '높이뛰기'와는 다른 종목이에요. 발음은 [장대노피뛰기]예요.
explain_en: It is a track-and-field event in which you clear a bar with the help of a long pole. It differs from '높이뛰기' (high jump), which is jumping without a pole. It is pronounced [장대노피뛰기].

examples.en: There is a big mansion on the hill.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 넓은 저택에서 살아요.
examples.en: The main character in the movie lives in a spacious mansion.

examples.ko: 이 저택은 백 년 전에 지어졌어요.
examples.en: This mansion was built a hundred years ago.
A rich man bought a mansion and decorated the garden.

examples.ko: 저택 안에는 방이 스무 개나 있대요.
examples.en: I heard there are twenty rooms inside the mansion.

examples.ko: 저택 주변에는 높은 담이 쳐져 있어요.
examples.en: A high wall surrounds the mansion.

explain: '저택'은 크고 고급스러운 집이에요. 주로 영화, 드라마, 뉴스에서 들어요. 내 집을 저택이라고 하면 농담처럼 들려요. 평범한 집은 그냥 '집'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '저택' is a large, grand house, mostly heard in films, dramas and the news. Calling your own house a '저택' sounds like a joke. An ordinary home is just a '집'.

examples.en: This exam has a lot of open-ended questions.

examples.ko: 주관식은 답을 직접 써야 해서 어려워요.
examples.en: Open-ended questions are hard because you have to write the answer yourself.
It's harder to get points on open-ended questions than multiple-choice ones.

examples.ko: 주관식으로 답을 쓸 때는 글씨를 또박또박 써요.
examples.en: When I answer open-ended questions, I write clearly.
The last two questions are open-ended.
The teacher grades open-ended answers by hand.

explain: 반대말은 '객관식'이에요. 보기 중에서 고르지 않고 답을 직접 쓰는 문제를 말해요. 짧게 쓰는 '단답형', 길게 쓰는 '서술형'도 모두 주관식에 들어가요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '객관식' (multiple choice). It refers to questions where you write the answer yourself instead of choosing. Both short-answer '단답형' and essay-style '서술형' count as 주관식.

examples.ko: 창문에 철망이 달려 있어서 벌레가 안 들어와요.
examples.en: There is a wire mesh on the window, so bugs don't come in.
My grandfather fenced around the chicken coop with wire mesh.

examples.ko: 운동장 철망 너머로 공이 넘어가 버렸어요.
examples.en: The ball went over the wire fence at the playground.
I put the fish on a wire grill and grill it.
A cat stuck its face out through the wire mesh.

examples.ko: 낡은 철망에 구멍이 나서 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: There is a hole in the old wire mesh, so we need to fix it.

explain: 철사를 엮어 만든 그물 모양의 물건에 두루 쓰는 말이에요. '철조망'은 가시철사로 두른 울타리를 말할 때가 많아서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: This is a general word for things woven from wire in a net shape. '철조망' is often a fence made with barbed wire, so the two are different.

en: to explore; to go on an expedition

examples.en: I explore a new neighborhood every weekend.
The children explored a cave in the forest.
I like movies about exploring space.

examples.ko: 깊은 바다를 탐험하려면 특별한 장비가 필요해요.
examples.en: You need special equipment to explore the deep sea.

examples.ko: 지도 없이 섬을 탐험하다가 길을 잃었어요.
examples.en: I got lost exploring the island without a map.
There are so many places I want to explore.

explain: '여행하다'는 가는 것 자체를, '탐험하다'는 잘 모르는 곳을 위험이나 설렘을 느끼며 알아보러 가는 것을 말해요. 정글, 동굴, 우주처럼 낯선 곳에 잘 어울리고, 가벼운 말로 '동네를 탐험하다'처럼 재미있게도 써요. 명사는 '탐험'이에요.
explain_en: '여행하다' is simply traveling; 탐험하다 is going into an unfamiliar place to find out about it, with a sense of adventure or risk. It suits jungles, caves, and space, and is also used playfully, as in '동네를 탐험하다' (explore the neighborhood). The noun is '탐험'.

en: in fact; in truth; indeed; actually

examples.en: Come to think of it, that's true too.
Well, I thought so at first too.

examples.ko: 하기는 요즘 물가가 너무 올라서 이해가 가요.
examples.en: Then again, prices have gone up so much that I understand.

examples.ko: 하기는 비가 이렇게 오는데 누가 나가고 싶겠어요?
examples.en: Well, with rain like this, who would want to go out?

examples.ko: 하기는 제가 그 사람이라도 화가 났겠어요.
examples.en: Then again, I would have been angry too if I were him.

examples.ko: 하기는 그 식당은 값에 비해 양이 적어요.
examples.en: Well, that restaurant does give small portions for the price.

explain: 상대나 앞의 말을 '그러고 보니 맞네'라고 인정할 때 써요. 대화에서는 '하긴'으로 줄여 말하는 경우가 많아요. '편하기는 하지만'처럼 '-기는 하다' 구조에 들어간 '하기는'과는 달라요.
explain_en: Use it to concede that what was said is right when you think about it. In conversation it is often shortened to '하긴'. It is different from the '-기는 하다' pattern, as in '편하기는 하지만'.
